newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels Bel-20 index seen falling to 2,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Brussels Bel-20 index seen falling to 2,000 level.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, hit by a third day of profittaking on Thursday, is expected to fall 100 points further before stabilising as investors worry over a U.S. interest rate hike and a delay in European Economic and Monetary union (EMU).
"The Bel-20 will go down to 2,000 before it finds solid ground," said one trader.
The blue-chip Bel-20 fell 0.31 percent, or 6.54 points, to 2,132.12, but reduced its losses minutes before bourse close as the Dow Jones saw some recovery in its early Thursday trade.

"I thought 2,120 was the bottom, but it looks like it can fall further as it's still weak with interest rate worries in the U.S. and everyone in Europe talking about an EMU delay, more people will take profits," said another trader.
Investors are nervously awaiting the March 25 meeting of the policy-making committee of the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve, which sets U.S. interest rates.
There is concern that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates to keep a lid on inflation.
Traders said they welcomed the Bel-20 correction, adding that it had given the market a breather after recent bull runs.
Insurance group Royale Belge was the blue-chip's main loser, falling 2.14 percent to 8,700 francs.
"Royale Belge is down on profittaking after last week's rises, but volume was not very large," said trader Tim Rovencamp at brokerage Nedee & Co.
Another stock which suffered from profittaking fever was Belgium's fourth-largest bank BBL, closing down 1.6 percent at 7,970 francs. BBL had risen over 10 percent since one month ago.
Attention was also on Societe Generale de Belqique (SGB) which announced a 22 percent rise in 1996 profits after the bourse closed.
But SGB closed down 1.06 percent at 2,805 francs on profittaking.
